references.text: The same command to bind God's words as a sign on the hand and as a symbol between the eyes, given in connection with deliverance from Egypt
Repeats the command that the Lord's law should be as a sign on the hand and as a symbol on the forehead
Parallel text commanding that God's words be upon the heart, bound as a sign on the hand, and serve as symbols between the eyes
Moses exhorts the people to lay all these words upon their hearts and to command their children to keep them
Encouragement to bind kindness and truth around the neck and write them on the tablet of the heart
Bind your father's commands upon your heart and tie them around your neck
Keep the commands, bind them on your fingers, and write them on the tablet of your heart
The prophecy of the new covenant in which God writes His law within their hearts
Jesus notes that the Pharisees make their prayer straps broad, a practice based on the literal interpretation of this verse
Quotes the promise of the new covenant that God's laws will be written in their minds and upon their hearts
Repeats the promise that God will put His laws into their hearts and write them in their minds
